chunks: He said: "You will not be able to bear with me."
ai.seo_question: What did Allah tell Prophet Musa about his ability to be patient with Al-Khidr?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse establishes the epistemological distinction between *'ilm al-yaqin* (knowledge of certainty) possessed by the Prophets and the limited *'ilm al-'ayan* (knowledge of observation) of the common believer, highlighting Al-Khidr's unique status as a servant endowed with divine secret knowledge (*'ilm al-ladunni*). The phrase underscores the necessity of *sabr* (patient endurance) not merely as passive waiting, but as active trust in the hidden wisdom (*hikmah*) of Allah's decree, even when divine actions appear contradictory to human logic. This sets the stage for the three trials in Surah Al-Kahf, illustrating how surface-level injustice often conceals deeper, divinely ordained mercy.
